name: Credo Technology
fiscalYearEnd: Saturday closest to April 30 (FY2026 ended May 2, 2026)

logo.source: credosemi.com home page header logo (inline SVG in the nav__logo link); no Wikipedia article with an infobox logo was found

description: Credo is a fabless chip and cable company that sells the high-speed links inside AI data centers. Its biggest product is the Active Electrical Cable (AEC), a copper cable with a Credo chip in each end that connects GPUs, servers and switches within and between racks; it also sells optical-module DSP chips, PCIe retimers, SerDes chiplets, ZeroFlap optical transceivers and licenses its SerDes IP. Customers are hyperscalers, neoclouds and the cable and module makers that supply them, who buy mostly on purchase orders with no long-term commitments. Revenue rose from $437M to $1,335M in FY2026 mainly because AEC shipments ramped at hyperscale customers, and two customers were 49% and 32% of revenue. TSMC makes all its wafers.

sub.name: Data-center networking, servers, optics and cooling

hq.note: Operating headquarters in the San Francisco Bay Area; San Jose is the first property listed in Item 2. Registered mailing address is c/o Maples Corporate Services, Grand Cayman (FY2026 10-K cover).

employees.note: 807 full-time equivalents, of whom 616 were engineers; 330 in North America and 477 in Asia (FY2026 10-K)

businessLines.name: Active Electrical Cables (ZeroFlap AECs)
businessLines.how: One-time hardware sale per cable on customer purchase orders, with Credo's chip as the high-margin part; volume follows hyperscaler and neocloud AI rack build-outs, and cables are built by contract manufacturer BizLink.
businessLines.description: Plug-and-play copper cables with Credo chips in the connectors, 100G to 800G and emerging 1.6T, up to 7 m, replacing passive copper cables (DACs) and active optical cables (AOCs) inside AI racks.
businessLines.revenueNote: Not reported by product. The FY2026 10-K MD&A says AEC unit shipments at hyperscale customers contributed over 99% of the $898.3M revenue increase; Q1 FY2027 10-Q says AEC contributed over 90% of the $255.9M increase.

businessLines.name: ICs: optical DSPs, PCIe retimers and line-card PHYs
businessLines.how: Chips sold per unit to optical-module makers, OEMs and ODMs on purchase orders; wins are design-ins that ship as the customer's module or board ramps.
businessLines.description: Seventh-generation PAM4 optical DSPs (50G to 200G per lane, including Linear Receive Optics parts), Toucan PCIe 6/CXL 3 retimers, and OmniConnect / Weaver memory fanout chips.

businessLines.name: SerDes chiplets and IP licensing
businessLines.how: Chiplets are sold per unit; IP is licensed to a customer for a fee, turning a custom design into a licensable block.
businessLines.description: SerDes chiplets (for example 3.2 Tbps) for multi-chip modules and licensing of Credo's SerDes IP.
businessLines.revenueNote: Not reported separately in the FY2026 10-K; the filing says IP solutions consist primarily of SerDes IP licensing

brands.name: ZeroFlap AEC (CLOS, SPAN, SHIFT, SWITCH families)
brands.share: Not reported separately; AEC drove over 99% of FY2026 revenue growth

brands.name: Hyperlume, Inc.
brands.segment: microLED interconnect subsidiary acquired in FY2026
brands.share: Pre-revenue development; owns 16 of Credo's 39 pending US patent applications (FY2026 10-K). Hyperlume and CoMira Solutions acquired together for $112.9M cash.

whatsNext.text: 200G-per-lane electrical PAM4 links planned for mass deployment by hyperscale customers in 2027
